qt: to the Commission Marko Vešligaj (S&D) Subject:

Regulation (EU) 2026/1768 amended Article 80 of Regulation (EU) 2021/2115 to clarify that working capital, including stand-alone working capital, may constitute eligible expenditure under common agricultural policy interventions. Article 68 of Regulation (EU) 2021/1060 provides that, in the case of financial instruments in the form of loans, eligible expenditure corresponds to payments to final recipients. There is a need to clarify whether, in cases where a financial instrument provides a loan to a farmer for the purpose of financing eligible working capital, the principal amount of that loan disbursed to the final recipient may itself be considered eligible expenditure for the purposes of the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development contribution. 1.

Does the Commission consider that the principal amount of a loan disbursed to a final recipient through a financial instrument may constitute eligible expenditure under Article 80 of Regulation (EU) 2021/2115, read in conjunction with Article 58 of Regulation (EU) 2021/1060, where the loan is used to finance eligible working capital, including stand-alone working capital?

Could the Commission clarify whether the loan principal actually disbursed to the farmer may be included as eligible expenditure for the purposes of the EU contribution to the financial instrument, irrespective of the subsequent repayment of that principal by the final recipient?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.11.2026) Under Article 3(4), point (b) of Regulation (EU) 2021/2115 (the Regulation)1, an ‘operation’ in the context of financial instruments supported by the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD) is the total eligible public expenditure granted to a financial instrument and the subsequent financial support provided to final recipients by that instrument. Article 80(5) of the Regulation sets out the rules on the eligibility of expenditure for EAFRDsupported financial instruments, mirroring Article 68(1) of Regulation (EU) 2021/10602. For loans, the eligible expenditure corresponds to payments to final recipients made within the eligibility period3. The amount recognised as eligible expenditure is the total eligible public expenditure paid, comprising the Union contribution and public co-financing, but excluding the additional national financing referred to in Article 115(5) of the Regulation. Therefore, loans financing working capital, including stand-alone working capital not linked to an investment, are subject to the same rules on the eligibility of expenditure under Article 80(5) as loans for investments. The specific provisions on working-capital finance under paragraphs 3 and 4 of Article 80also apply. The eligibility of a loan granted under an EAFRD-supported financial instrument is linked to its disbursement to the final recipient provided that the final recipient meets the applicable eligibility conditions defined in the respective strategic plan, drawn up by the Member State under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) Strategic Plan and in the Funding Agreement, at the time of granting the loan. The repayment of the loan and its frequency do not play a role in determining the eligibility.
